    Validate all historical files, then apply the pending batch in one transaction under a database-wide advisory lock.

accept_backoff(prev_ns: int) -> int
    The pause after a failed accept: 5ms, doubling to 1s while it keeps failing.
listen_and_serve[S](r: Router[S], port: int) -> result[int, str]
    Bind, then accept until the process is asked to stop.
listen_and_serve_with[S](r: Router[S], port: int, sc: ServerConfig) -> result[int, str]
    Same, with timeouts, limits, and the shutdown drain window under the caller's control -- built from config with...

## sio_serve.sl -- Socket.IO routes, served: Engine.IO v4 and Socket.IO v5 (what socket.io-client 3 and 4 speak), on both of its transports.
gc struct SioRoute[S] { settings: SioSettings, event: fn(S, Socket, SioEvent), connect: opt[fn(S, Socket, str, str) -> result[bool, str]], disconnect: opt[fn(S, Socket, str, str)], sessions: SioSessions }
sio_route[S](event: fn(S, Socket, SioEvent)) -> SioRoute[S]
SioRoute.on_connect(f: fn(S, Socket, str, str) -> result[bool, str]) -> SioRoute[S]
SioRoute.on_disconnect(f: fn(S, Socket, str, str)) -> SioRoute[S]

## socket.sl -- A live connection the serve loop holds open after an upgrade, and the hub that lets one connection's handler reach the others.
gc struct Socket { id: str, route: str, protocol: str, client_ip: str, locals: map[str]str, lock: mutex, out: chan[Out], open: bool, ended: str, close_code: int, close_reason: str, hubs: [Hub], namespaces: map[str]bool, handler: int, handshake: http.Response, sio: bool, accepted: bool }
Socket.send_text(s: str) -> bool
    Queues a text message.
Socket.send_binary(b: bytes) -> bool
Socket.emit(namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str) -> bool
    Socket.IO: `emit(name, ...args)` on a namespace ("/" by default).
Socket.emit_with_ack(namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, id: int) -> bool
    The same, asking the client to acknowledge: its answer arrives as an Ack event carrying `id`.
Socket.ack(namespace: str, id: int, args_json: str) -> bool
    The answer to a client event that asked for one (SioEvent.ack >= 0).
Socket.emit_binary(namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, data: [bytes]) -> bool
    emit with binary attachments: `args_json` is the other arguments, as for emit, and each of `data` follows them as a binary...
Socket.disconnect_ns(namespace: str) -> bool
    Disconnects the client from one namespace; the session stays.
Socket.close(code: int, reason: str) -> bool
    Starts the closing handshake with `code` (1000 normal, 1001 going away, 1008 policy, 4000-4999 the application's own) and...
Socket.is_open() -> bool
Socket.local(key: str) -> str
    A value the handshake's hooks set on the request, "" when none did.
Socket.set_local(key: str, v: str) -> int
gc struct Hub { id: str, lock: mutex, sockets: map[str]Socket, rooms: map[str]map[str]bool }
    Sockets by id, and rooms of them: what a chat, a live dashboard or a notification fan-out needs to reach more than the one...
new_hub() -> Hub
Hub.add(s: Socket) -> int
Hub.remove(s: Socket) -> int
    Takes the socket out of the hub and every room in it.
Hub.join_room(s: Socket, room: str) -> int
    Puts the socket in a room (adding it to the hub first if needed).
Hub.leave_room(s: Socket, room: str) -> int
Hub.count() -> int
Hub.room_size(room: str) -> int
Hub.get(id: str) -> opt[Socket]
    The socket with this id, if it is in the hub.
Hub.broadcast(text: str, except: str) -> int
    Text to every WebSocket in the hub but `except` (an id, or "").
Hub.broadcast_binary(b: bytes, except: str) -> int
Hub.to_room(room: str, text: str, except: str) -> int
Hub.to_room_binary(room: str, b: bytes, except: str) -> int
Hub.emit_all(namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, except: str) -> int
    Socket.IO: one event to every Socket.IO session in the hub, encoded once.
Hub.emit_to_room(room: str, namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, except: str) -> int
Hub.emit_binary_to_room(room: str, namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, data: [bytes], except: str) -> int
    emit_binary to every Socket.IO session in a room ("" for the hub).

## testkit.sl -- Building a request, and reading a response.
gc struct TestRequest { method: Method, path: str, headers: map[str]str, body: bytes }
request(method: Method, path: str) -> TestRequest
get_request(path: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.header(name: str, value: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.bearer(token: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.basic(credentials: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.content_type(ct: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.body_str(body: str) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.body_bytes(body: bytes) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.json_body(body: str) -> TestRequest
    Sets the content type too, because a body without one is a body a real client would not send.
TestRequest.json(body: Json) -> TestRequest
TestRequest.multipart(boundary: str, fields: map[str]str, files: [Upload]) -> TestRequest
    A multipart body, built from the parts given: each file is `name:filename:content-type:content`, each field `name:value`.
TestRequest.build() -> http.Request
    Not fallible: a header that fails http.request()'s validation (CR or LF in a name or value, a colon in a name) here is a bug...
upload_part(field: str, filename: str, content_type: str, content: str) -> Upload
    One part for `multipart`, without going near a real encoder.
resp_status(r: http.Response) -> int
    `status_of` is taken by the registry, so responses read as `resp_status`, `resp_text`, `resp_header`, `resp_json`.
resp_text(r: http.Response) -> str
resp_header(r: http.Response, name: str) -> str
resp_json(r: http.Response) -> Json
    The body as JSON, or Null when it is not JSON at all -- so an assertion reads `json_of(resp).get("id")` without a guard.
resp_error_code(r: http.Response) -> str
    The error code in zokor's envelope: "not_found", "validation_failed".
resp_error_fields(r: http.Response) -> [str]
    The field names an error envelope complains about, in order, so a test asserts on the shape rather than on an exact string.

## tokens.sl -- Opaque bearer tokens.
gc struct TokenStore { subjects: map[str]str, expires: map[str]int, ttl: int, lock: mutex, since_sweep: int }
new_token_store(ttl_ns: int) -> TokenStore
    `ttl_ns` is how long a token stays valid after it is issued, in nanoseconds; 0 means until it is revoked.
new_token() -> result[str, str]
    32 random bytes as 64 lowercase hex characters.
TokenStore.issue(subject: str) -> result[str, str]
    A new token for `subject`.
TokenStore.issue_at(subject: str, now: int) -> result[str, str]
TokenStore.lookup(token: str) -> opt[str]
    The subject a live token was issued to; none for an unknown, revoked or expired token (an expired one is dropped on the way).
TokenStore.lookup_at(token: str, now: int) -> opt[str]
TokenStore.revoke(token: str) -> bool
    Ends one token (logout).
TokenStore.revoke_subject(subject: str) -> int
    Ends every token issued to `subject` ("log out everywhere", a password change).
TokenStore.count() -> int
    How many tokens are held (expired ones count until swept).
bearer_subject[S](c: Ctx[S], store: TokenStore) -> opt[str]
    The subject behind the request's `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or none when the header is missing or the token is not live.

## tracing.sl -- Request-scoped W3C context, carried explicitly across tasks and calls.
gc struct TraceConfig { max_parent_bytes: int, max_state_bytes: int, max_state_members: int }
    Startup limits for incoming W3C headers.
gc struct Tracer { max_parent_bytes: int, max_state_bytes: int, max_state_members: int }
    Validated, immutable startup tracing settings.
struct TraceContext { trace_id: str, parent_id: str, span_id: str, sampled: bool, state: str }
    Explicit request context; pass this value when spawning background work.
trace_config() -> TraceConfig
    Default limits: 256 parent bytes, 512 state bytes, 32 state members.
new_tracer(cfg: TraceConfig) -> result[Tracer, str]
    Validate all startup limits together and copy them.
trace_context(t: Tracer, headers: bytes) -> result[TraceContext, str]
    Invalid, absent or duplicate parents start a new trace.
trace_header(ctx: TraceContext) -> result[str, str]
    A validated version-00 header; reserved flags are always zero.
trace_request(ctx: TraceContext, req: httpc.Request) -> result[httpc.Request, str]
    Copy the request and its headers; never mutate a shared caller request.
trace_registry(reg: Registry, ctx: TraceContext) -> Registry
    Bind a registry by copying its startup references, never changing the shared registry as concurrent requests arrive with...
struct TraceLogger { logger: Logger, trace_id: str, request_id: str }
    A request binding over a shared Logger, without changing its configuration.
traced_logger(log: Logger, ctx: TraceContext) -> TraceLogger
    Bind application records to a validated trace id.

## upload.sl -- File uploads.
gc struct UploadRules { limits: multipart.Limits, allowed_types: [str], allowed_extensions: [str], require_content_type: bool }
gc struct Upload { field: str, filename: str, raw_filename: str, content_type: str, data: bytes }
gc struct Form { values: map[str]str, files: [Upload] }
gc struct FormError { code: str, detail: str }
    The reason a form was refused: a registered error code, and a sentence naming what was wrong.
default_uploads() -> UploadRules
uploads_allowing(types: [str]) -> UploadRules
with_max_file_bytes(r: UploadRules, n: int) -> UploadRules
with_max_total_bytes(r: UploadRules, n: int) -> UploadRules
with_max_files(r: UploadRules, n: int) -> UploadRules
with_extensions(r: UploadRules, exts: [str]) -> UploadRules
parse_form(content_type: str, body: bytes, rules: UploadRules) -> result[Form, FormError]
value(f: Form, name: str) -> str
has_value(f: Form, name: str) -> bool
file(f: Form, field: str) -> opt[Upload]
    The first file posted under a field name, which is the usual case.
files_for(f: Form, field: str) -> [Upload]
    Every file under one field name: `<input multiple>` posts repeats.
total_bytes(f: Form) -> int
safe_filename(raw: str) -> str
    A client's filename, made safe to use as ONE path segment.
extension_of(filename: str) -> str
    ".png" for "a.png", lowercased; "" when there is no extension.
media_type_of(header: str) -> str
    The media type without its parameters: "image/png" from "image/png; charset=binary".

## ws.sl -- WebSocket, and Socket.IO on top of it.
gc struct WsRules { max_frame_bytes: int, max_message_bytes: int, protocols: [str], ping_interval: int, pong_timeout: int, max_queue: int, close_timeout: int }
default_ws() -> WsRules
ws_allowing(protocols: [str]) -> WsRules
enum Incoming { Text, Binary, Ping, Pong, Close }
gc struct Message { kind: Incoming, text: str, data: bytes, code: int, reason: str }
gc struct Conn { rules: WsRules, inbox: builder.Bytes, have: int, need: int, partial: builder.Bytes, partial_op: ws.Op, fragmenting: bool, outbox: bytes, closed: bool, sid: str }
new_conn(rules: WsRules) -> Conn
is_upgrade(req: http.Request) -> bool
    Is this request asking to become a WebSocket? Cheap enough to call on every request, so a route can serve both.
upgrade(req: http.Request, rules: WsRules) -> result[http.Response, str]
    The 101 to send back, or the failure to report.
receive(c: Conn, chunk: bytes) -> result[[Message], str]
    Feeds bytes in and takes whole messages out.
pending(c: Conn) -> bytes
    Bytes the connection owes the peer (pongs, the close echo), taken out: call it after `receive` and write whatever it returns.

gc struct SioSettings { ping_interval_ms: int, ping_timeout_ms: int, max_payload: int, max_polling_sessions: int, max_attachments: int }

    The first thing a socket.io connection needs: its session id and the keepalive timings, as a text frame.

    Turns one WebSocket text message into a socket.io event.

## ws_serve.sl -- WebSocket routes, served: the handshake goes through the router like any request -- its `before`s run, so authentication and...
gc struct WsRoute[S] { rules: WsRules, message: opt[fn(S, Socket, Message)], closed: opt[fn(S, Socket, int, str)], sio: opt[SioRoute[S]] }
ws_route[S](rules: WsRules, message: fn(S, Socket, Message)) -> WsRoute[S]
    The message handler is the one a route cannot do without; on_close is optional.
WsRoute.on_close(f: fn(S, Socket, int, str)) -> WsRoute[S]
    Called once when the connection ends, however it ended, with the code and reason: the peer's, the ones this side closed with,...

## internal/multipart (reached as UploadRules.limits)
gc struct Limits { max_parts: int, max_files: int, max_file_bytes: int, max_field_bytes: int, max_total_bytes: int, max_headers_bytes: int, max_filename_bytes: int }


# Examples

> Explore runnable Slang examples built with Zokor, from a minimal HTTP service to WebSocket chat and testable ports and fakes.

- [Hello service](hello.html) — make example

- [Chat service](chat.html) — make example-chat

- [Ports and fakes](ports.html) — make example-ports


# Hello service

> A minimal Slang HTTP service built with Zokor. See how to configure the server, register a route, and return a JSON response.

# Hello service

A zokor service.

Run from the repository root: `make example`.

## `examples/hello/main.sl`

```slang
// A zokor service.
//
// Read the "the service" section below: that is the whole API, and it
// ends at `listen_and_serve`. The section after that is a client, not a
// server: it makes the same requests a curl would, over a real socket,
// so this file demonstrates the service by running it rather than by
// describing it.
import "http";
import "httpc";
import "time";
import "../../zokor" as zokor;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //
// the service                                                        //
// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //

gc struct App {
    name: str,
    requests: int,
    token: str,
}

fn home(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    return zokor.text(200, "hello from " + c.state.name);
}

fn search(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    return zokor.text(200, "q=" + c.query("q") +
                           " page=" + to_str(c.query_int("page", 1)));
}

fn show_org(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    let _who = c.local("user_id");     // put there by require_token
    if c.param("id") != "7" {
        return zokor.respond_with(c.errors, "org.not_found",
                                  "no such organisation '" + c.param("id") + "'",
                                  c.request_id);
    }
    return zokor.ok_json("{\"org\":\"7\"}");
}

// A DTO: a declared shape. `zokor.dto` fills it (slang's own
// json.decode underneath), a missing field is an error rather than a
// silent zero, and the field it names is already in the envelope.
gc struct CreateOrg {
    name: str,
    plan: str,
    seats: i32,
    website: opt[str],
}

fn create_org(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    // the wire is camelCase, the struct is snake_case: no tags needed,
    // and a decode failure is already the response to return
    let r: result[CreateOrg, http.Response] = zokor.dto(c);
    guard let dto = r else let resp = err_of(r) {
        return resp;
    }

    // types are checked by the decoder; VALUES are checked here, and
    // every problem is reported at once
    let v = zokor.checker();
    if len(dto.name) == 0 {
        v.note("name", "must not be empty");
    }
    if dto.seats < 1 || dto.seats > 500 {
        v.note("seats", "must be between 1 and 500");
    }
    if dto.plan != "free" && dto.plan != "pro" {
        v.note("plan", "must be one of: free, pro");
    }
    if v.failed() {
        return zokor.respond_fields(c.errors, "validation_failed",
                                    v.fields, c.request_id);
    }

    let body = zokor.jobj()
        .set_str("id", "org_7")
        .set_str("name", dto.name)
        .set_str("plan", dto.plan)
        .set_int("seats", dto.seats as int)
        .set_opt_str("website", dto.website);
    return zokor.created(zokor.camel_keys(body.render()), "/orgs/org_7");
}

// A shape nobody declared: a webhook whose fields belong to somebody
// else. `json_body` walks it without a struct.
fn webhook(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    let r = c.json_body();
    guard let body = r else let e = err_of(r) {
        return zokor.respond_with(c.errors, e.code, e.detail,
                                  c.request_id);
    }
    let event = body.get("type").str_or("unknown");
    let city = body.path("data.customer.address.city").str_or("nowhere");
    let first_item = body.path("data.items.0.sku").str_or("none");
    return zokor.ok_json(zokor.jobj()
        .set_str("event", event)
        .set_str("city", city)
        .set_str("first_item", first_item)
        .set_int("item_count", body.path("data.items").size())
        .render());
}

fn asset(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    return zokor.text(200, "file " + c.param("rest"));
}

// An upload: the rules say what is acceptable, and anything else comes
// back as a registered failure rather than reaching this handler.
fn upload_avatar(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    let rules = zokor.with_max_file_bytes(
        zokor.uploads_allowing(["image/png", "image/jpeg"]), 1048576);
    let r = c.upload(rules);
    guard let form = r else let e = err_of(r) {
        return zokor.respond_with(c.errors, e.code, e.detail,
                                  c.request_id);
    }
    guard let avatar = zokor.file(form, "avatar") else {
        return zokor.respond_with(c.errors, "validation_failed",
                                  "no file was posted under 'avatar'",
                                  c.request_id);
    }
    // avatar.filename is already safe to use as one path segment
    return zokor.ok_json("{\"stored\":\"" + avatar.filename +
                         "\",\"type\":\"" + avatar.content_type +
                         "\",\"bytes\":" + to_str(len(avatar.data)) +
                         ",\"title\":\"" + zokor.value(form, "title") + "\"}");
}

// Middleware. A `before` may end the request, or resolve something and
// hand it to the handler through the context; an `after` sees whatever
// response came back, including one a before produced.
//
// Note what is NOT here: a list of public paths. This hook is attached
// to a group, so it only ever runs for the routes inside it.
fn require_token(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> opt[http.Response] {
    if c.bearer() != c.state.token {
        return some(zokor.respond(c.errors, "unauthorized",
                                  c.request_id));
    }
    // resolved once, at the edge, instead of in every handler
    c.set_local("user_id", "u_1");
    return none;
}

fn count(c: zokor.Ctx[App], r: http.Response) -> http.Response {
    c.state.requests = c.state.requests + 1;
    return zokor.with_header(r, "x-request-count", to_str(c.state.requests));
}

// Configuration is read once, here, and validated before anything runs.
let cfg = zokor.load_config();          // base, profile, startup environment

let app = App {
    name: zokor.str_or(cfg, "SERVICE_NAME", "hello"),
    requests: 0,
    token: zokor.str_or(cfg, "API_TOKEN", "s3cret")
};

// new_router's own registry, carried onto every Ctx from here on --
// register the app's own codes on top of the built-ins it already has.
let r = zokor.new_router(app);
zokor.register(r.errors, "org.not_found", 404, "no such organisation");

// public: no authentication
r.get("/", home);
r.get("/search", search);
r.get("/files/*rest", asset);

// everything under /api needs a token, and says so once
let api = r.group("/api");
api.before(require_token);
api.get("/orgs/:id", show_org);
api.post("/orgs", create_org);
api.post("/avatars", upload_avatar);
api.post("/webhooks/stripe", webhook);

// counted for every request, public or not
r.after(count);


// The whole server, from here on. `listen_and_serve` accepts and spawns
// one task per connection; it returns when the process is asked to stop.
// A real service calls it and nothing else -- the spawn here is only so
// this file can also play the client below.
//
// It would also log every request (README, "Logging"). The client below
// prints each exchange itself and the program ends the moment it is done,
// so this demo turns the log off rather than interleave the two; a real
// service keeps it.
let sc = zokor.default_server_config();
sc.logger = zokor.no_logger();
spawn zokor.listen_and_serve_with(r, port(), sc);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //
// the demo: a real client, over a real socket                        //
//                                                                    //
// Nothing below is part of zokor's API -- it is here so `make check`  //
// exercises the server end to end rather than describing it.         //
// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //

// A function, not a top-level `let`: the client helpers below are
// functions, and a top-level binding is local to the main task.
fn port() -> int {
    return 18080;
}

fn base() -> str {
    return "http://127.0.0.1:" + to_str(port());
}

fn deadline() -> until {
    return until_of(time.mono() + 5000000000);
}

fn send(rq: httpc.Request) -> httpc.Response {
    let c = httpc.new_client();
    let r2 = httpc.client_send(c, rq, deadline());
    guard let resp = r2 else let e = err_of(r2) {
        println("request failed: " + e);
        exit(1);
    }
    return resp;
}

// Every request carries its own X-Request-Id, which the server reuses
// (it is well-formed): the ids in the envelopes below are this one, so
// the output is the same on every run instead of a fresh random id each.
fn call(method: str, p: str, token: str, body: str, ctype: str) -> httpc.Response {
    let rq = httpc.new_request(method, base() + p);
    rq.headers["x-request-id"] = "example-req-1";
    if len(token) > 0 {
        rq.headers["authorization"] = "Bearer " + token;
    }
    if len(body) > 0 {
        rq.headers["content-type"] = ctype;
        rq.body = to_bytes(body);
    }
    return send(rq);
}

fn get(p: str) -> httpc.Response {
    return call("GET", p, "", "", "");
}

fn json_call(method: str, p: str, token: str, body: str) -> httpc.Response {
    return call(method, p, token, body, "application/json");
}

fn show(label: str, resp: httpc.Response) {
    println(label + " -> " + to_str(resp.status) + " " + to_str(resp.body));
}

// wait for the listener to be up before the first request
fn wait_ready() {
    let i = 0;
    while i < 200 {
        let c = httpc.new_client();
        let r2 = httpc.client_get(c, base() + "/", deadline());
        guard let _ok = r2 else {
            time.sleep(10000000);
            i = i + 1;
            continue;
        }
        return;
    }
    println("server never came up");
    exit(1);
}

wait_ready();

println("routes:");
for line in r.routes_list() {
    println("  " + line);
}
println("");

show("GET    /", get("/"));
show("GET    /search?q=slang&page=2", get("/search?q=slang&page=2"));
show("GET    /api/orgs/7", call("GET", "/api/orgs/7", "s3cret", "", ""));
show("GET    /api/orgs/9", call("GET", "/api/orgs/9", "s3cret", "", ""));
show("GET    /api/orgs/7 (no token)", get("/api/orgs/7"));
show("POST   /api/orgs (empty body)", call("POST", "/api/orgs", "s3cret", "", ""));
show("POST   /api/orgs (bad values)",
     json_call("POST", "/api/orgs", "s3cret",
               "{\"name\":\"\",\"plan\":\"gold\",\"seats\":0}"));
show("POST   /api/orgs (wrong type)",
     json_call("POST", "/api/orgs", "s3cret",
               "{\"name\":\"acme\",\"plan\":\"pro\",\"seats\":\"many\"}"));
show("POST   /api/orgs (missing field)",
     json_call("POST", "/api/orgs", "s3cret", "{\"name\":\"acme\"}"));
show("POST   /api/orgs",
     json_call("POST", "/api/orgs", "s3cret",
               "{\"name\":\"acme\",\"plan\":\"pro\",\"seats\":12,\"website\":\"https://acme.test\"}"));
show("POST   /api/webhooks/stripe",
     json_call("POST", "/api/webhooks/stripe", "s3cret",
               "{\"type\":\"invoice.paid\",\"data\":{\"customer\":{\"address\":{\"city\":\"Lagos\"}},\"items\":[{\"sku\":\"A1\"},{\"sku\":\"B2\"}]}}"));

let avatar = "--B\r\n" +
    "Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"title\"\r\n\r\n" +
    "My avatar\r\n" +
    "--B\r\n" +
    "Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"avatar\"; filename=\"../../etc/passwd.png\"\r\n" +
    "Content-Type: image/png\r\n\r\n" +
    "PNGDATA\r\n" +
    "--B--\r\n";
show("POST   /avatars",
     call("POST", "/api/avatars", "s3cret", avatar,
          "multipart/form-data; boundary=B"));

let bad_avatar = "--B\r\n" +
    "Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"avatar\"; filename=\"x.svg\"\r\n" +
    "Content-Type: image/svg+xml\r\n\r\n" +
    "<svg/>\r\n" +
    "--B--\r\n";
show("POST   /avatars (svg)",
     call("POST", "/api/avatars", "s3cret", bad_avatar,
          "multipart/form-data; boundary=B"));

show("GET    /files/a/b.txt", get("/files/a/b.txt"));
show("HEAD   /", call("HEAD", "/", "", "", ""));
show("DELETE /api/orgs/7", call("DELETE", "/api/orgs/7", "s3cret", "", ""));
show("BREW   /", call("BREW", "/", "", "", ""));
show("GET    /nope", call("GET", "/nope", "s3cret", "", ""));
println("");
// one more than the calls above: wait_ready's probe is a request
// like any other, and the `count` hook counts every one.
println("requests served: " + to_str(app.requests));
```


# Chat service

> A Slang chat service using Zokor, with WebSocket and Socket.IO clients connected to the same room.

# Chat service

A chat service: the same room for WebSocket clients and socket.io clients, on one server.

Run from the repository root: `make example-chat`.

## `examples/chat/main.sl`

```slang
// A chat service: the same room for WebSocket clients and socket.io
// clients, on one server.
//
//     slangc examples/chat/main.sl --run            the scripted demo below
//     slangc examples/chat/main.sl --run -- serve   a real server on :8080
//
// With `serve`, point a browser at it:
//
//     const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080/ws?name=ada", "chat");
//     ws.onmessage = (m) => console.log(m.data);
//     ws.send("hello");
//
//     const socket = io("http://localhost:8080", { query: { name: "leo" } });
//     socket.on("chat message", (m) => console.log(m));
//     socket.emit("chat message", "hi", (reply) => console.log(reply));
//
// Read "the service": that is everything a real one writes. The demo after
// it is a stand-in browser -- real connections to a real server on a free
// port -- so `make example-chat` shows the exchange without one.
import "http";
import "proc";
import "time";
import "../../zokor" as zokor;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //
// the service                                                        //
// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //

gc struct App {
    name: str,
    // everyone in the chat, WebSocket and socket.io alike
    hub: zokor.Hub,
    history: [str],
    lock: mutex,
}

fn remember(app: App, line: str) {
    mutex_lock(app.lock);
    push(app.history, line);
    mutex_unlock(app.lock);
}

// The handshake, for both kinds of client. Every `before` has run by now
// (an auth hook would have set c.local("user")); this one only wants a name.
fn arrive(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    let name = c.query("name");
    if name == "" {
        return zokor.respond_with(c.errors, "unauthorized", "say who you are: ?name=",
                                  c.request_id);
    }
    let s = c.socket();
    s.set_local("name", name);
    c.state.hub.join_room(s, "chat");
    return c.accept_ws();
}

// WebSocket clients: every text message goes to the room.
fn on_text(app: App, s: zokor.Socket, m: zokor.Message) {
    if m.kind != zokor.Incoming.Text {
        s.send_text("only text, please");
        return;
    }
    if m.text == "/history" {
        mutex_lock(app.lock);
        let h = join_lines(app.history);
        mutex_unlock(app.lock);
        s.send_text(h);
        return;
    }
    let line = s.local("name") + ": " + m.text;
    remember(app, line);
    // to WebSocket clients as text, to socket.io clients as an event
    app.hub.to_room("chat", line, s.id);
    app.hub.emit_to_room("chat", "/", "chat message", zokor.jstr(line).render(), s.id);
}

fn on_ws_close(app: App, s: zokor.Socket, code: int, reason: str) {
    remember(app, s.local("name") + " left (" + to_str(code) + ")");
}

// socket.io clients.
fn on_event(app: App, s: zokor.Socket, e: zokor.SioEvent) {
    if e.kind != zokor.SioKind.Event {
        return;
    }
    if e.name == "chat message" {
        remember(app, s.local("name") + " said " + e.args_json);
        app.hub.emit_to_room("chat", e.namespace, "chat message", e.args_json, s.id);
        let said = "";
        let pr = zokor.parse(e.args_json);
        if let args = pr {
            said = args.at(0).str_or("");
        }
        app.hub.to_room("chat", s.local("name") + ": " + said, s.id);
        if e.ack >= 0 {
            // the client used socket.emit(..., callback)
            s.ack(e.namespace, e.ack, "[\"delivered\"]");
        }
        return;
    }
    s.emit(e.namespace, "error", "\"unknown event: " + e.name + "\"");
}

fn on_sio_leave(app: App, s: zokor.Socket, ns: str, why: str) {
    remember(app, s.local("name") + " left " + ns + " (" + why + ")");
}

fn chat_router(app: App) -> zokor.Router[App] {
    let r = zokor.new_router(app);
    r.websocket("/ws", arrive,
                zokor.ws_route(zokor.ws_allowing(["chat"]), on_text).on_close(on_ws_close));
    r.socketio("/socket.io/", arrive,
               zokor.sio_route(on_event).on_disconnect(on_sio_leave));
    return r;
}

fn join_lines(xs: [str]) -> str {
    let out = "";
    let i = 0;
    while i < len(xs) {
        if i > 0 {
            out = out + " | ";
        }
        out = out + xs[i];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return out;
}

fn new_app() -> App {
    return App { name: "zokor chat", hub: zokor.new_hub(), history: [], lock: make_mutex() };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //
// the demo: a stand-in browser, printed                              //
//                                                                    //
// Real connections to the server above. Nothing below is part of     //
// zokor's API: a browser does all of this for you.                   //
// ---------------------------------------------------------------- //

import "../../zokor/internal/ws" as frames;

fn soon() -> until {
    return until_of(time.mono() + 2000000000);
}

// A client's frames are masked, which the server requires.
fn client_frame(op: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes {
    let n = len(payload);
    let head: bytes = b"..";
    head[0] = 128 | op;
    head[1] = 128 | n;
    let key = b"\x2a\x07\x63\x01";
    let body = b"";
    let one: bytes = b".";
    let i = 0;
    while i < n {
        one[0] = payload[i] ^ key[i % 4];
        body = body + one;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    return head + key + body;
}

fn says(c: &mut link, s: str) {
    let _s = c.send_bytes(client_frame(1, to_bytes(s)), soon());
}

fn bye(c: &mut link) {
    let b: bytes = b"..";
    b[0] = 3;
    b[1] = 232;
    let _s = c.send_bytes(client_frame(8, b), soon());
}

// Sends the upgrade request and returns the status line; whatever came
// after the response head is kept in `got`.
gc struct Inbox {
    got: bytes,
}

fn open(c: &mut link, path: str, box: Inbox) -> str {
    let req = "GET " + path + " HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\n" +
              "Connection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n" +
              "Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==\r\n" +
              "Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: chat\r\n\r\n";
    let _s = c.send_bytes(to_bytes(req), soon());
    let a = arena_new(4096);
    let w = a.wire(4096);
    let got = b"";
    while true {
        let rr = c.recv(w, soon());
        guard let n = rr else { return "no answer"; }
        if n == 0 { return "closed"; }
        got = got + to_bytes(w[0..n]);
        let i = 0;
        while i + 3 < len(got) {
            if got[i] == 13 && got[i + 1] == 10 && got[i + 2] == 13 && got[i + 3] == 10 {
                box.got = got[i + 4..len(got)];
                let j = 0;
                while got[j] != 13 { j = j + 1; }
                return to_str(got[0..j]);
            }
            i = i + 1;
        }
    }
    return "no answer";
}

// The next frame from the server, printed as a browser would see it.
fn hears(label: str, c: &mut link, box: Inbox) {
    let a = arena_new(4096);
    let w = a.wire(4096);
    while true {
        let dr = frames.decode(box.got, 0, 1048576, false);
        guard let d = dr else { println(label + " <- (undecodable)"); return; }
        if d.kind == frames.Decoded.Frame {
            let f = d.frame;
            box.got = box.got[f.size..len(box.got)];
            if f.op == frames.Op.Text {
                println(label + " <- " + to_str(f.payload));
            } else if f.op == frames.Op.Close {
                let cr = frames.decode_close(f.payload);
                if let body = cr {
                    println(label + " <- close " + to_str(body.code) + " " + body.reason);
                } else {
                    println(label + " <- close");
                }
            } else {
                println(label + " <- frame " + to_str(frames.code_of(f.op)));
            }
            return;
        }
        let rr = c.recv(w, soon());
        guard let n = rr else { println(label + " <- (nothing)"); return; }
        if n == 0 { println(label + " <- (connection closed)"); return; }
        box.got = box.got + to_bytes(w[0..n]);
    }
}

fn serve_all(ln: link, r: zokor.Router[App]) {
    let sc = zokor.default_server_config();
    sc.logger = zokor.no_logger();
    let mut_ln = ln;
    while true {
        let ar = mut_ln.accept(until_never());
        guard let c = ar else { return; }
        spawn zokor.serve_conn(r, c, sc);
    }
}

// Waits until the server has finished with a client that left, so the
// history printed at the end is complete.
fn settle(app: App, lines: int) {
    let waited = 0;
    while waited < 200 {
        mutex_lock(app.lock);
        let n = len(app.history);
        mutex_unlock(app.lock);
        if n >= lines { return; }
        time.sleep(10000000);
        waited = waited + 1;
    }
}

fn demo() {
    let app = new_app();
    let r = chat_router(app);
    let lr = link_listen(0);
    guard let ln = lr else { panic("cannot listen"); }
    let port = ln.port();
    spawn serve_all(ln, r);

    println("websocket:");
    let ada = link_dial("127.0.0.1", port, soon()) ?? panic_link();
    let ab = Inbox { got: b"" };
    println("  ada  handshake -> " + open(&mut ada, "/ws?name=ada", ab));
    let bo = link_dial("127.0.0.1", port, soon()) ?? panic_link();
    let bb = Inbox { got: b"" };
    println("  bo   handshake -> " + open(&mut bo, "/ws?name=bo", bb));
    let anon = link_dial("127.0.0.1", port, soon()) ?? panic_link();
    let nb = Inbox { got: b"" };
    println("  anon handshake -> " + open(&mut anon, "/ws", nb));
    says(&mut ada, "hello");
    hears("  bo  ", &mut bo, bb);
    says(&mut bo, "hi ada");
    hears("  ada ", &mut ada, ab);
    println("");

    println("socket.io:");
    let leo = link_dial("127.0.0.1", port, soon()) ?? panic_link();
    let lb = Inbox { got: b"" };
    println("  leo  handshake -> " +
            open(&mut leo, "/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket&name=leo", lb));
    // the session id is random; the rest of the open packet is not
    let a = arena_new(4096);
    let w = a.wire(4096);
    let opened = false;
    while !opened {
        let dr = frames.decode(lb.got, 0, 1048576, false);
        guard let d = dr else { break; }
        if d.kind == frames.Decoded.Frame {
            let f = d.frame;
            lb.got = lb.got[f.size..len(lb.got)];
            let text = to_str(f.payload);
            let at = 0;
            let tb = to_bytes(text);
            while at < len(tb) && tb[at] != 44 { at = at + 1; }
            println("  leo  <- 0{\"sid\":\"...\"" + to_str(tb[at..len(tb)]));
            opened = true;
        } else {
            let rr = a_recv(&mut leo, w);
            lb.got = lb.got + rr;
        }
    }
    says(&mut leo, "40");
    let _ok = skip_one(&mut leo, lb);
    println("  leo  -> 40           (connected to /)");
    says(&mut leo, "421[\"chat message\",\"hi from socket.io\"]");
    hears("  ada ", &mut ada, ab);
    hears("  bo  ", &mut bo, bb);
    hears("  leo ", &mut leo, lb);
    says(&mut ada, "and back");
    hears("  bo  ", &mut bo, bb);
    hears("  leo ", &mut leo, lb);
    says(&mut leo, "42[\"whatever\"]");
    hears("  leo ", &mut leo, lb);
    println("");

    println("leaving:");
    bye(&mut ada);
    hears("  ada ", &mut ada, ab);
    settle(app, 5);
    says(&mut leo, "41");
    settle(app, 6);
    says(&mut bo, "/history");
    hears("  bo  ", &mut bo, bb);
}

fn a_recv(c: &mut link, w: wire) -> bytes {
    let rr = c.recv(w, soon());
    guard let n = rr else { return b""; }
    return to_bytes(w[0..n]);
}

// The CONNECT answer carries the random session id too: read past it.
fn skip_one(c: &mut link, box: Inbox) -> bool {
    let a = arena_new(4096);
    let w = a.wire(4096);
    while true {
        let dr = frames.decode(box.got, 0, 1048576, false);
        guard let d = dr else { return false; }
        if d.kind == frames.Decoded.Frame {
            box.got = box.got[d.frame.size..len(box.got)];
            return true;
        }
        let rr = c.recv(w, soon());
        guard let n = rr else { return false; }
        if n == 0 { return false; }
        box.got = box.got + to_bytes(w[0..n]);
    }
    return false;
}

fn panic_link() -> link {
    panic("cannot connect");
}

let args = proc.args();
if len(args) > 1 && args[len(args) - 1] == "serve" {
    let r = chat_router(new_app());
    let sr = zokor.listen_and_serve(r, 8080);
    guard let _ok = sr else let e = err_of(sr) {
        println(e);
        exit(1);
    }
} else {
    demo();
}
```


# Ports and fakes

> A runnable Slang example showing how to isolate dependencies behind ports and test Zokor services with fakes.

# Ports and fakes

The example source files are shown below.

Run from the repository root: `make example-ports`.

## `examples/ports/src/application/inventory/ports.sl`

```slang
import "../../domain/inventory" as stock;

// C is explicit adapter state: function fields never capture credentials or globals.
pub gc struct StockPort[C] {
    context: C,
    lookup: fn(C, str, str) -> result[opt[stock.Stock], str],
}
```

## `examples/ports/src/application/inventory/service.sl`

```slang
import "../../domain/inventory" as stock;
import "strings";

pub gc struct Service[C] { port: StockPort[C] }

pub fn new_service[C](port: StockPort[C]) -> Service[C] { return Service[C] { port: port }; }

// Tenant identity is resolved at the edge and passed through every port call.
pub fn find[C](service: Service[C], tenant_id: str, sku: str) -> result[opt[stock.Stock], str] {
    let checked = stock.key(tenant_id, sku);
    guard let _key = checked else let e = err_of(checked) { return err(e); }
    let lookup = service.port.lookup;
    let loaded = lookup(service.port.context, tenant_id, sku);
    guard let maybe = loaded else let e = err_of(loaded) { return err(e); }
    if let row = maybe {
        if row.tenant_id != tenant_id || row.sku != sku { return err("adapter returned a different tenant_id or sku"); }
        if row.available < 0 { return err("adapter returned a negative available count"); }
    }
    return ok(maybe);
}

// Share the domain rule with the HTTP edge without importing adapters.
pub fn valid_sku(sku: str) -> bool { return stock.identifier(sku); }
```

## `examples/ports/src/domain/inventory/stock.sl`

```slang
import "strings";

pub struct Stock { tenant_id: str, sku: str, available: int }

pub fn identifier(value: str) -> bool {
    if len(value) < 1 || len(value) > 64 { return false; }
    for ch in to_bytes(value) {
        if !((ch >= 65 && ch <= 90) || (ch >= 97 && ch <= 122) ||
             (ch >= 48 && ch <= 57) || ch == 45 || ch == 95) { return false; }
    }
    return true;
}

// The separator cannot occur in either identifier: tenant keys stay distinct.
pub fn key(tenant_id: str, sku: str) -> result[str, str] {
    let problems: [str] = [];
    if !identifier(tenant_id) { push(problems, "tenant_id must contain 1..64 ASCII letters, digits, - or _"); }
    if !identifier(sku) { push(problems, "sku must contain 1..64 ASCII letters, digits, - or _"); }
    if len(problems) > 0 { return err(strings.join(problems, "; ")); }
    return ok(tenant_id + ":" + sku);
}

pub fn new_stock(tenant_id: str, sku: str, available: int) -> result[Stock, str] {
    let problems: [str] = [];
    let checked = key(tenant_id, sku);
    if let _key = checked {} else let e = err_of(checked) { push(problems, e); }
    if available < 0 { push(problems, "available must be nonnegative"); }
    if len(problems) > 0 { return err(strings.join(problems, "; ")); }
    return ok(Stock { tenant_id: tenant_id, sku: sku, available: available });
}
```

## `examples/ports/src/infrastructure/memory/client.sl`

```slang
import "../../application/inventory" as inventory;
import "../../domain/inventory" as stock;
import "strings";

// Seed once at startup; immutable afterwards, so readers do not need a lock.
pub gc struct Store { stocks: map[str]stock.Stock }

pub fn new_store(rows: [stock.Stock]) -> result[Store, str] {
    let values: map[str]stock.Stock = {};
    let problems: [str] = [];
    let i = 0;
    for row in rows {
        let made = stock.new_stock(row.tenant_id, row.sku, row.available);
        guard let checked = made else let e = err_of(made) {
            push(problems, "rows[" + to_str(i) + "]: " + e); i += 1; continue;
        }
        let key = stock.key(checked.tenant_id, checked.sku) ?? "";
        if has(values, key) { push(problems, "rows[" + to_str(i) + "]: duplicate tenant_id and sku"); }
        else { values[key] = checked; }
        i += 1;
    }
    if len(problems) > 0 { return err(strings.join(problems, "; ")); }
    return ok(Store { stocks: values });
}

pub fn lookup(ctx: Store, tenant_id: str, sku: str) -> result[opt[stock.Stock], str] {
    let checked = stock.key(tenant_id, sku);
    guard let key = checked else let e = err_of(checked) { return err(e); }
    if !has(ctx.stocks, key) { let absent: opt[stock.Stock] = none; return ok(absent); }
    return ok(some(ctx.stocks[key]));
}

pub fn new_stock_port(ctx: Store) -> inventory.StockPort[Store] {
    return inventory.StockPort[Store] { context: ctx, lookup: lookup };
}
```

## `examples/ports/src/interfaces/web/router.sl`

```slang
import "../../../../../zokor" as zokor;
import "../../application/inventory" as inventory;
import "http";
import "json";

pub fn register_errors(errors: zokor.Registry) {
    zokor.register(errors, "inventory.not_found", 404, "stock not found");
    zokor.register(errors, "inventory.unavailable", 503, "inventory is unavailable");
}

// The route wrapper resolves authentication and passes explicit values here.
pub fn show[C](service: inventory.Service[C], tenant_id: str, sku: str,
               errors: zokor.Registry, request_id: str) -> http.Response {
    if !inventory.valid_sku(sku) {
        return zokor.respond_fields(errors, "validation_failed",
            [zokor.field("sku", "must contain 1..64 ASCII letters, digits, - or _")], request_id);
    }
    let loaded = inventory.find(service, tenant_id, sku);
    guard let maybe = loaded else { return zokor.respond(errors, "inventory.unavailable", request_id); }
    guard let row = maybe else { return zokor.respond(errors, "inventory.not_found", request_id); }
    return zokor.ok_json(json.encode(row));
}
```

## `examples/ports/src/main.sl`

```slang
// Startup wiring is the only package that knows the concrete adapter.
import "application/inventory" as inventory;
import "domain/inventory" as stock;
import "infrastructure/memory" as memory;
import "interfaces/web" as rest;
import "../../../zokor" as zokor;
import "http";

gc struct App { inventory: inventory.Service[memory.Store], tokens: zokor.TokenStore }
fn require_tenant(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> opt[http.Response] {
    guard let tenant_id = zokor.bearer_subject(c, c.state.tokens) else {
        return some(zokor.respond(c.errors, "unauthorized", c.request_id));
    }
    c.set_local("tenant_id", tenant_id);
    return none;
}
fn show_stock(c: zokor.Ctx[App]) -> http.Response {
    return rest.show(c.state.inventory, c.local("tenant_id"), c.param("sku"), c.errors, c.request_id);
}

fn main() {
    let cfg = zokor.load_config();
    let count = zokor.int_or(cfg, "EXAMPLE_STOCK", 7);
    let checked = zokor.check(cfg);
    guard let _config = checked else let e = err_of(checked) { println(e); exit(1); }
    let made = stock.new_stock("tenant_a", "pen", count);
    guard let row = made else let e = err_of(made) { println(e); exit(1); }
    let seeded = memory.new_store([row]);
    guard let adapter = seeded else let e = err_of(seeded) { println(e); exit(1); }
    let service = inventory.new_service(memory.new_stock_port(adapter));
    let tokens = zokor.new_token_store(0);
    let issued = tokens.issue("tenant_a");
    guard let token = issued else { println("token issue failed"); exit(1); }
    let router = zokor.new_router(App { inventory: service, tokens: tokens });
    rest.register_errors(router.errors);
    router.before(require_tenant);
    router.get("/stock/:sku", show_stock);
    // Drive the same handler pipeline hermetically. A server passes router to listen_and_serve.
    let denied = router.serve(zokor.get_request("/stock/pen").build());
    println("unauthenticated -> " + to_str(denied.status));
    let found = router.serve(zokor.get_request("/stock/pen").bearer(token).build());
    println("stock -> " + to_str(found.status) + " " + zokor.resp_text(found));
    let missing = router.serve(zokor.get_request("/stock/missing").bearer(token).build());
    println("missing -> " + to_str(missing.status) + " " + zokor.resp_error_code(missing));
}
main();
```
